title: Kind of Blue
label: Columbia
description: The calmest revolution in jazz: Davis, Coltrane, Cannonball Adderley and Bill Evans improvising over sparse modal sketches. Unhurried, late-night and endlessly replayable. This is an early stereo pressing, the kind collectors hunt for.

copies.notes: Early stereo pressing, light ring wear on the cover.

title: Kind of Blue
label: Columbia/Legacy
description: A modern 180-gram reissue of the modal jazz landmark. Quiet vinyl and an affordable way to own the record every jazz shelf starts with.

title: Blue Train
label: Blue Note
description: Coltrane's only Blue Note session as a leader: a three-horn front line, Lee Morgan's bright trumpet and the famous title blues. Muscular hard bop with gorgeous Rudy Van Gelder sound. Original mono pressing, a true rarity.

copies.notes: Original mono, deep groove. Kept behind the counter.

title: Blue Train
label: Blue Note
description: An audiophile all-analog reissue in a heavy gatefold sleeve. For most listeners it sounds superb and costs a tiny fraction of an original; collectors still chase the 1957 pressing for its history.

title: A Love Supreme
label: Impulse!
description: A four-part suite of devotion and intensity, from a chanted bass motif to Coltrane's searing solos. One of the most personal statements in jazz.

title: Somethin' Else
label: Blue Note
description: Cannonball's date with Miles Davis as a sideman. The slow, smoky 'Autumn Leaves' is the reason many people fall for jazz in the first place.

title: Moanin'
label: Blue Note
description: Gospel-tinged call and response, Blakey's thunderous drums and a band that swings hard. If Kind of Blue is midnight, this is the lively hour before it.

title: The Sidewinder
label: Blue Note
description: A funky, boogaloo-flavoured title track that became a surprise hit, followed by sharp, upbeat hard bop. A great next step for anyone who loves Kind of Blue but wants more swagger.

copies.notes: Surface noise on quiet passages, plays through.

title: Mingus Ah Um
label: Columbia
description: Raucous gospel shouts, tender ballads and sly satire from jazz's great bassist and composer. Includes the moving tribute 'Goodbye Pork Pie Hat'.

tracklist.title: Better Git It in Your Soul

title: The Epic
label: Brainfeeder
description: Nearly three hours of big-band spiritual jazz with choir and strings. Proof that jazz on vinyl is very much alive: cinematic, generous and a lot of fun.

title: Head Hunters
label: Columbia
description: Hancock's turn toward funk: long, hypnotic grooves built on synths, clavinet and a tight rhythm section. The record that made jazz-funk a genre.

copies.notes: Light surface marks, plays with some crackle.

title: Head Hunters
label: Columbia/Legacy
description: A clean modern reissue of the jazz-funk classic. Same grooves, no crackle, half the price of a good original.

title: Thrust
label: Columbia
description: The Head Hunters band one year later: tighter, spacier and full of synthesizer colour. 'Actual Proof' is a drummer's favourite.

title: Black Byrd
label: Blue Note
description: Trumpeter Byrd teams up with producer Larry Mizell for smooth, sunny jazz-funk that later fed countless hip-hop samples.

title: Everybody Loves the Sunshine
label: Polydor
description: Warm vibraphone, lazy summer grooves and one of the most sampled title tracks ever. Sounds like a hot afternoon.

title: What's Going On
label: Tamla
description: A seamless song cycle about war, poverty and the planet, sung with heartbreaking tenderness. Soul music growing up.

tracklist.title: Inner City Blues (Make Me Wanna Holler)

title: Songs in the Key of Life
label: Tamla
description: A double album plus bonus EP, overflowing with joy, funk and ambition. 'Sir Duke', 'Isn't She Lovely' and 'As' on one set.

title: Super Fly
label: Curtom
description: A film soundtrack that outgrew its film: wah-wah guitars, lush strings and sharp social commentary in Curtis's falsetto.

title: Mothership Connection
label: Casablanca
description: George Clinton's space-age funk at its peak: huge horns, rubbery bass and 'Give Up the Funk'. Party records don't get better.

tracklist.title: P. Funk (Wants to Get Funked Up)
Give Up the Funk (Tear the Roof off the Sucker)

title: Lady Soul
label: Atlantic
description: The Queen of Soul in full command: 'Chain of Fools', '(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman' and gospel fire throughout.

tracklist.title: (You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman
Since You've Been Gone (Sweet Sweet Baby)
Good to Me as I Am to You

title: Zombie
label: Coconut
description: Relentless Afrobeat groove and biting satire of military obedience. Long, hypnotic tracks built for dancing and protest at the same time.

title: Abbey Road
label: Apple
description: The last album the Beatles recorded together, closing with the famous side-two medley. Warm, polished and full of Harrison's best songs. UK original pressing.

tracklist.title: You Never Give Me Your Money
She Came In Through the Bathroom Window

title: Abbey Road
label: Apple
description: The 50th-anniversary edition with a new stereo mix: clearer vocals and punchier drums than the old masters. A great first copy.

tracklist.title: You Never Give Me Your Money
She Came In Through the Bathroom Window

title: Rumours
label: Warner Bros.
description: Breakup songs written by a band breaking up, polished into perfect pop-rock. 'Dreams', 'Go Your Own Way' and 'The Chain' on one side of history.

title: Fleetwood Mac
label: Reprise
description: The first album with Buckingham and Nicks, where the classic line-up's magic begins. 'Rhiannon' and 'Landslide' live here.

title: Tusk
label: Warner Bros.
description: The strange, sprawling follow-up to Rumours: Buckingham's lo-fi experiments next to Nicks and McVie's gems. A double album that rewards patience.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
label: Harvest
description: Time, money, madness and a heartbeat holding it all together. The ultimate headphone album, here as a UK original with posters.

tracklist.title: The Great Gig in the Sky

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
label: Pink Floyd Records
description: The remastered 180-gram reissue: dead-quiet vinyl and the full gatefold art. The easy way to hear why this record never left the charts.

tracklist.title: The Great Gig in the Sky

title: Led Zeppelin IV
label: Atlantic
description: Riffs, mandolins and mythology: 'Black Dog', 'Stairway to Heaven' and John Bonham's colossal drums on 'When the Levee Breaks'.

title: A Night at the Opera
label: EMI
description: Queen's grand, theatrical masterpiece, from music-hall whimsy to the operatic 'Bohemian Rhapsody'. Gatefold UK original.

tracklist.title: I'm in Love with My Car

title: Nevermind
label: DGC
description: The album that dragged underground rock into the mainstream. Original 1991 vinyl is scarce because most copies sold on CD and cassette.

title: The Bends
label: Parlophone
description: Big guitars and bigger feelings: the bridge between Radiohead's early rock and everything strange that followed. 'Fake Plastic Trees' still floors people.

title: OK Computer
label: Parlophone
description: Anxious, beautiful and eerily prophetic about life with technology. The original double LP is one of the most sought-after records of the 90s.

title: Kid A
label: Parlophone
description: Radiohead swap guitars for glitchy electronics and buried vocals. Cold on first listen, then impossible to stop playing.

title: In Rainbows
label: XL Recordings
description: Radiohead at their warmest: intricate rhythms, gentle melodies and 'Weird Fishes/Arpeggi'. The pay-what-you-want album that is worth owning on wax.

title: Unknown Pleasures
label: Factory
description: Bleak, spacious and electrifying: Martin Hannett's production turned a Manchester punk band into something ghostly. Iconic pulsar cover.

title: Unknown Pleasures
label: Factory
description: A remastered 180-gram reissue that keeps the textured sleeve. The original's dark atmosphere without the original's price tag.

title: Love Will Tear Us Apart
label: Factory
description: The single that outlived the band: a danceable song about heartbreak, released weeks after Ian Curtis's death. Original 7-inch.

title: An Ideal for Living
label: Enigma
description: The band's raw, self-released debut EP, still closer to punk than to the sound that made them famous. A genuine collector's rarity.

title: Remain in Light
label: Sire
description: New wave meets Fela Kuti: interlocking polyrhythms, Brian Eno's production and 'Once in a Lifetime'. Nervous, joyful and endlessly danceable.

tracklist.title: Born Under Punches (The Heat Goes On)

title: Marquee Moon
label: Elektra
description: Two guitars weaving crystalline lines around each other. Born in the CBGB punk scene, but closer to jazz in spirit; the title track is ten minutes of bliss.

title: Loveless
label: Creation
description: Walls of bent, blurred guitar and whispered melodies. The defining shoegaze record, best played loud.

title: Autobahn
label: Philips
description: A 22-minute synthesizer drive down the motorway that pointed the way to synth-pop and techno. German original pressing.

title: Trans-Europe Express
label: Kling Klang
description: Mechanical rhythms, melancholy melodies and a train journey across a continent. Its title track became the backbone of early hip-hop and electro.

title: Blue Monday
label: Factory
description: The best-selling 12-inch single of its era, in the famous die-cut floppy-disk sleeve. Drum machine, bass hook, pure dancefloor.

title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
label: Apollo
description: Bedroom-made techno that floats as much as it pulses. Hazy, melodic and strangely emotional; a cornerstone of ambient electronic music.

title: Music Has the Right to Children
label: Warp
description: Wobbly analog synths and hip-hop beats that sound like half-remembered childhood films. Nostalgic and a little unsettling.

title: Discovery
label: Virgin
description: Filtered disco, vocoder pop and pure joy: 'One More Time', 'Digital Love' and 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger'.

title: Illmatic
label: Columbia
description: Ten tracks, no filler: a young Queensbridge poet over beats by Premier, Pete Rock and Q-Tip. The benchmark for lyrical hip-hop.

title: The Low End Theory
label: Jive
description: Upright bass, jazz samples and effortless back-and-forth between Q-Tip and Phife. Where hip-hop and jazz shook hands.

title: 3 Feet High and Rising
label: Tommy Boy
description: Playful, colourful and packed with samples, from Steely Dan to Hall & Oates. A daisy-age antidote to tough-guy rap.

title: Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
label: Loud
description: Gritty, kung-fu-film-sampling beats from RZA and nine wildly different MCs. Raw, murky and hugely influential.

title: Donuts
label: Stones Throw
description: Thirty-one short, looping soul-sample sketches finished by a producer near the end of his life. Warm, wonky and deeply moving.

title: To Pimp a Butterfly
label: Top Dawg Entertainment
description: Hip-hop steeped in jazz, funk and spoken word, with Thundercat and Kamasi Washington in the band. Dense, political and musical.

title: Bach: The Goldberg Variations
label: Columbia Masterworks
description: The debut that made a young Canadian pianist famous overnight: fast, crisp and full of energy. Original mono pressing.

title: Bach: The Goldberg Variations (1981 Recording)
label: CBS Masterworks
description: Gould returns to the Goldbergs a lifetime later: slower, deeper and reflective. Fascinating side by side with his 1956 debut.

title: Elgar: Cello Concerto
label: HMV
description: A twenty-year-old du Pré with Barbirolli and the LSO, in the performance that still defines this concerto. Paired with Janet Baker's Sea Pictures.

title: Tabula Rasa
label: ECM New Series
description: Bell-like, slowly unfolding music of great stillness. The record that introduced Pärt's 'tintinnabuli' style to the world.

tracklist.title: Cantus in Memory of Benjamin Britten

title: Catch a Fire
label: Island
description: The album that carried roots reggae to the world: militant lyrics, deep grooves and 'Stir It Up'.

tracklist.title: Baby We've Got a Date (Rock It Baby)

title: Georgian Voices
label: Nonesuch
description: Georgian polyphonic singing at its most powerful: three-part harmonies, dissonant chords and ancient table songs. Nothing else sounds like it.
